title: Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: All employees of the James Hardie Group, plus consultants and contractors designated as Insiders by the Compliance Officer. Subject to the Black-out Period ban, the general Dealing prohibition, the ban on hedging unvested equity at any time, and a permission to hedge vested equity in an Open Period on 7 days' post-notification.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, plus employees designated as such by or on behalf of the General Counsel or Compliance Officer; expressly includes the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Financial Controller and Vice Presidents. Subject to an absolute ban on Hedging Transactions and Short Swing Profit Dealings, and to written pre-clearance on five ASX trading days' notice.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of James Hardie Industries SE. A subset of Designated Persons, distinguished only by the additional obligation to notify the Company of changes in their relevant interest within two ASX trading days for Appendix 3Y lodgment, and by the exemption approver being the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member likely to act on the Insider's instructions or Advice; a member of the Insider's family sharing the household; a family company (a company in which the Insider, domestic partner, relative or family trust is a director, shareholder or adviser); and any trust or estate in which the Insider is trustee, beneficiary, director of a trustee or adviser. Every prohibition is expressed as binding the Insider 'and his or her Associates'.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.

windows.end_anchor: two Australian Securities Exchange trading days after any results announcement by the Company

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to any results announcement, where the Company is purchasing its own Securities through a Buy-back
windows.end_anchor: 2 trading days after any results announcement by the Company

windows.start_anchor: two Australian Securities Exchange trading days after a quarterly profit announcement has been released to the market

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Compliance Officer (the General Counsel, or if unavailable the Company Secretary) may prohibit some or all Insiders and their Associates from Dealing in specific Securities or Company Securities, and may further prohibit one or more groups of Insiders and Associates from Dealing during certain periods, including Open Periods. All such decisions must be recorded in the Compliance Officer's register. The Board may also determine Black-out Periods 'or such other time as determined by the Board from time to time'. The policy does not say whether these prohibitions are confidential, but Insiders may inspect the register only to the extent it concerns them.

rules.section: 2 (Short Swing Profit and Hedging Transaction Prohibition); 16 (Hedging Transaction)
rules.detail: Any dealing in call or put options over Company Securities, or in other derivative Company Securities providing a means to limit economic risk, is a Hedging Transaction and is banned outright for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no vesting-state, venue or window carve-out and no notification alternative. A derivative that does not limit economic risk is still a Security and therefore a Dealing requiring written pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.

rules.section: 2 (Short Swing Profit and Hedging Transaction Prohibition)
rules.detail: Non-Designated Insiders and their Associates may not deal in puts, calls or other risk-limiting derivatives over unvested shares, options, RSUs or any other employee equity-based compensation, at any time.
rules.evidence: a Hedging Transaction of unvested shares, options, restricted stock units or any other instrument provided as employee equity-based compensation at any time.

rules.detail: A non-Designated Insider or Associate may deal in puts, calls or other derivative Company Securities over vested equity or Company Securities, but only within an Open Period, only if not in possession of Inside Information and not the subject of a Compliance Officer prohibition, and must notify the Compliance Officer within 7 days after the Dealing. No venue restriction is imposed, so an OTC option is within the permission.
rules.evidence: An Insider or one of his or her Associates (other than a Designated Person) wishing to Deal in Company Securities through a Hedging Transaction of vested shares, options, restricted stock units, any other instrument provided as employee equity-based compensation or Company Securities may only do so if such Dealing is within the Open Period and the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.

rules.section: 2 (Short Swing Profit and Hedging Transaction Prohibition)
rules.detail: Absolute, permanent ban on Hedging Transactions by Designated Persons (all Directors, CEO, CFO, Financial Controller, Vice Presidents) and their Associates, covering vested and unvested equity and Company Securities generally. The only relief is a specific exemption under Section 6.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.

rules.section: 2 (Short Swing Profit and Hedging Transaction Prohibition)
rules.detail: Hedging of unvested employee equity-based compensation is banned at all times for non-Designated Insiders and their Associates; there is no Open Period or notification route for unvested holdings.
rules.evidence: An Insider (other than a Designated Person) or one of his or her Associates must not engage in: (a) a Hedging Transaction of unvested shares, options, restricted stock units or any other instrument provided as employee equity-based compensation at any time.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested employee equity and of Company Securities generally is prohibited 'except as permitted in Section 3', which allows it inside an Open Period with post-notification to the Compliance Officer within 7 days. No pre-approval is required for this tier, and no minimum shareholding floor is imposed.
rules.evidence: a Hedging Transaction of vested shares, options, restricted stock units, any other instrument provided as employee equity-based compensation or Company Securities, except as permitted in Section 3.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar that limits the economic risk of Company Securities falls within the Hedging Transaction definition and is therefore banned outright for Designated Persons. An outright sale of vested shares is not a Hedging Transaction and remains available in an Open Period with written pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation over vested holdings by a non-Designated Insider is treated as a Hedging Transaction: permitted only within an Open Period, without Inside Information, with notification to the Compliance Officer within 7 days after the Dealing.
rules.evidence: may only do so if such Dealing is within the Open Period and the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere named and is not listed in the definition of Deal. A short position taken to limit the economic risk of a holding would in substance be caught by the Hedging Transaction ban for Designated Persons, but the policy itself does not say so.
Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the Deal definition, which reaches buying, selling, otherwise trading in, gifting, pledging, accepting and exercising Securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial instrument whose value is partly determined by the value of Company Securities and so a Security and a Dealing; where it provides a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities it is a Hedging Transaction and is banned outright for this tier.
rules.evidence: in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.

rules.detail: For non-Designated Insiders a CFD over Company Securities is a Dealing in a Security. It may be entered in an Open Period without Inside Information and without a Compliance Officer prohibition; if it limits economic risk it is also a Hedging Transaction and attracts the 7-day notification, and the unvested hedging ban if it hedges unvested equity.
rules.evidence: An Insider and his or her Associates may Deal in Company Securities during an Open Period, but only if at that time: (a) the Insider or Associate is not in possession of Inside Information; and (b) the Compliance Officer has not prohibited such Insider or Associates from Dealing in the Company Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named and is not prohibited. Pledging Securities is expressly within the definition of Deal, so putting Company Securities up as margin collateral is a Dealing: it must occur in an Open Period, outside a Black-out Period, without Inside Information, and requires written approval by the Compliance Officer on not less than five ASX trading days' notice. The policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls and price triggers.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: For non-Designated Insiders a margin loan pledge is a Dealing that may be done in an Open Period without Inside Information; no pre-clearance or notification is required unless the Insider is in doubt and applies under Section 10.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: Granting a pledge over Company Securities is not separately prohibited but is expressly a Deal, so for Designated Persons it needs written Compliance Officer approval on five ASX trading days' notice, must be executed in the Open Period following approval and outside any Black-out Period, and subsequent confirmation must be given. Charges, liens and mortgages other than pledges are not named.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: A pledge by a non-Designated Insider is a Dealing permitted in an Open Period absent Inside Information or a Compliance Officer prohibition; pledging unvested plan securities is not separately addressed, though such securities are usually not transferable under the plan rules.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing, margin loans or loans in respect of Company Securities. The financing itself is not a Dealing, but the security granted over the shares is (pledging), so the transaction requires written pre-clearance for Designated Persons and must be executed within the Open Period following approval. No disclosure of financing arrangements is required beyond confirmation of the Dealing and, for Directors, Appendix 3Y notification of relevant-interest changes.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: Secured financing is not addressed for non-Designated Insiders either; the pledge leg is a Dealing that may be done in an Open Period without Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: Designated Persons and their Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit, defined as profit realised or expected to be realised from any purchase and sale, or sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months. Because Securities include derivatives, matched derivative legs within six months are caught. No carve-out is stated for plan acquisitions.
rules.evidence: Short Swing Profit means any profit realised or expected to be realised by any Designated Person or any of his or her Associates from any purchase and sale, or any sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months.

rules.detail: The Short Swing Profit prohibition applies only to Designated Persons; no holding period or speculative-dealing rule is imposed on other Insiders.

clearance.approver: Compliance Officer (the General Counsel of the Company, or if he or she is not available the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Subsequent confirmation of the Dealing must be provided')
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons must advise the Company in writing directed to the Compliance Officer of any intended Dealing in Company Securities by such Designated Persons or their Associates, including any Dealing during any Open Period, not less than five Australian Securities Exchange trading days before the date of that intended Dealing. ... If the Compliance Officer approves the intended Dealing, such Dealing must take place within the Open Period following the approval (or such other period specified by the Compliance Officer)

clearance.approver: Compliance Officer for pre-clearance; the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee for any specific exemption
clearance.post_trade_to: the Company, for lodgment of an Appendix 3Y with the Australian Securities Exchange
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Australian Securities Exchange trading days of the change in relevant interest
clearance.evidence: All Directors must also notify the Company within two Australian Securities Exchange trading days of any changes to their relevant interest in Company Securities so that the Company can notify the Australian Securities Exchange of such changes through lodgment of an Appendix 3Y.

clearance.approver: Compliance Officer (only where the Insider is in doubt and applies under Section 10, or for equity plan applications and disposals under Section 3)
clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance Officer, for any Hedging Transaction of vested equity or Company Securities
clearance.evidence: the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.

short_term.basis: any purchase and sale, or any sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months
short_term.evidence: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.

exceptions.approver: CFO or General Counsel; for a Director or direct report to the CEO, the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee; all exemptions reported to the Board
exceptions.evidence: An exemption will only be granted if the Company is satisfied that there are good reasons that a prohibition should be waived, for instance employee hardship, and such approval will not undermine the underlying spirit of the Policy and applicable securities laws.

exceptions.approver: Compliance Officer (written advance approval), and the dealing must take effect in an Open Period
exceptions.evidence: Deal in Company Securities by exercising options or selling vested restricted shares or any other instrument provided solely or primarily for the benefit of employees of the James Hardie Group

exceptions.approver: Compliance Officer (written advance approval); application must take effect during an Open Period
exceptions.evidence: apply for Company Securities under a superannuation scheme, pension fund, option plan, restricted stock unit plan or other scheme established solely or primarily for the benefit of employees of the James Hardie Group
If the Company is purchasing its own Securities through a Buy-back, an employee of the James Hardie Group may Deal in Company Securities only: (a) if the Company is not in a Black-out Period

financing_disclosure: Designated Persons; inception of any pledge (a pledge is a Deal); Compliance Officer; written notice not less than five ASX trading days before the intended Dealing, plus subsequent confirmation of the Dealing
Directors; any resulting change to their relevant interest in Company Securities; the Company, for ASX Appendix 3Y lodgment; within two ASX trading days

exemption_authority: An employee may request a specific exemption from the Section 2 prohibitions (including the Hedging Transaction and Short Swing Profit bans), setting out reasons and the Section 7 information. An exemption is granted only if the Company is satisfied there are good reasons to waive the prohibition, for instance employee hardship, and that approval will not undermine the underlying spirit of the Policy and applicable securities laws. Approved by the CFO or General Counsel, or, for a Director or a direct report to the CEO, by the Chairman of the Board or the Audit Committee; all exemptions granted are reported to the Board. Other than exemptions expressly approved this way, 'there are no exceptions to this Policy'.
jurisdiction_overlays: Australia: Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) s 1043A insider trading, ss 182-183 improper use of information, s 1041A market manipulation, s 1041E false and misleading statements
United States: U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, U.S. Securities Act of 1933 and the rules, regulations and case law thereunder (the Short Swing Profit concept mirrors s 16(b))
Ireland: the Company is a Societas Europaea domiciled in Dublin and the appendices summarise Irish law

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedging ban for senior people
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are squarely a Hedging Transaction, so no director, CEO, CFO, Financial Controller or Vice President (or their family, family company or trust) can enter a collar at all, whether the shares are vested or not and whether the window is open or closed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging definition is economic, not instrument-based
bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It names call and put options directly and then sweeps in any other derivative that limits economic risk, so a bank cannot restructure the collar as a swap, prepaid forward or CFD to avoid it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exemption authority reaches the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee of the James Hardie Group may request a specific exemption from the prohibitions in Section 2 ... An exemption may be approved by the CFO or General Counsel, or in the case of an exemption for a Director or direct report to the CEO, by the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only route to a collar for a Designated Person: the hedging ban sits in Section 2 and is therefore waivable, but only on hardship-style 'good reasons', only if it does not undermine the spirit of the Policy, and the waiver is reported to the Board.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging permitted for non-designated staff on notification only
bespoke_clauses.clause: An Insider or one of his or her Associates (other than a Designated Person) wishing to Deal in Company Securities through a Hedging Transaction of vested shares ... may only do so if such Dealing is within the Open Period and the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Below Designated Person level a collar over vested shares is available with no pre-approval at all, provided it is struck inside the four-week Open Period and reported within 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited, but the security granted over the collared shares is itself a Dealing, so it must be struck in an Open Period and, for Designated Persons, pre-cleared in writing five ASX trading days in advance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no secured financing or margin lending ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, secured financing arrangements, forced sales by a lender, or price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy the funding leg is unrestricted in substance, so the obstacle to a funded collar here is entirely the hedge legs, not the loan.

bespoke_clauses.topic: short window and long lead time
bespoke_clauses.clause: Open Period means the period of four weeks following a quarterly profit announcement ... (such four-week period not beginning until two Australian Securities Exchange trading days after the announcement has been released to the market) ... not less than five Australian Securities Exchange trading days before the date of that intended Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a structure is permitted, the five-trading-day notice consumes a quarter of the four-week window, so pricing must be agreed well before the window opens and the trade re-priced on execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the Compliance Officer approves the intended Dealing, such Dealing must take place within the Open Period following the approval (or such other period specified by the Compliance Officer).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared pledge or unwind must settle before the Open Period closes, so a collar's roll, restrike or termination has to be scheduled against the quarterly calendar rather than a market date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short Swing Profit means any profit realised or expected to be realised by any Designated Person or any of his or her Associates from any purchase and sale, or any sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities include derivatives, even an exempted collar for a Designated Person could not be unwound, rolled or physically settled within six months of the opening legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means ... a family company of the Insider (i.e., a company in which an Insider, his or her domestic partner, a relative or family trust is a director, shareholder or adviser); or any trust or estate in which an Insider is a trustee, beneficiary or a director of a trustee or an adviser.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family company, family trust or an estate does not escape the Designated Person hedging ban, and the Insider must actively inform those persons of their obligations.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Compliance Officer may prohibit some or all Insiders and their Associates from Dealing in specific Securities ... The Compliance Officer may further prohibit one or more groups of Insiders and Associates from Dealing in Securities during certain periods, including Open Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An Open Period is not a guaranteed execution window: the Compliance Officer can close it for a group at any time, which must be treated as a condition precedent to pricing rather than a settled fact.

bespoke_clauses.clause: terminating or suspending an Insider's employment contract, and, if applicable, any such termination shall constitute a termination 'for cause' under such contract; or declaring the Insider ineligible for future participation in the James Hardie Group's equity incentive plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered by a Designated Person without an exemption is a for-cause termination event and forfeits future equity, so the bank should require written evidence of clearance or exemption before trading.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive of James Hardie without a specific exemption. Designated Persons, which expressly include all Directors, the CEO, CFO, Financial Controller and Vice Presidents, and their Associates 'must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time', and the Hedging Transaction definition names call and put options and any other derivative that limits the economic risk of Company Securities, so both collar legs are banned outright regardless of vesting state or window. The only route is a Section 6 specific exemption from the Section 2 prohibitions, granted by the CFO or General Counsel (or, for a Director or a direct report to the CEO, the Chairman of the Board or the Audit Committee) on hardship-style good reasons that do not undermine the spirit of the Policy, and reported to the Board. The funding leg is by contrast unconstrained: the policy says nothing about margin lending, secured financing, margin calls or forced sales, and the only requirement is that the pledge, being within the definition of Deal, be pre-cleared in writing five ASX trading days ahead and executed inside the four-week Open Period that starts two trading days after a quarterly announcement. Below Designated Person level a collar over vested shares is genuinely available, needing only an Open Period execution, no Inside Information, and notification to the Compliance Officer within 7 days after dealing.
